_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for RTO lead-assignment rules. Edit here only - three places read
this file and previously carried hand-copied duplicates of these values:
- scripts/lead_priority.py   (the Python cron that actually writes assignments)
- api/_lib/db.js             (awbPrefixRules, for leads recorded via the disposal path)
Kept under api/_lib/ specifically because deploy.yml bundles only api/ into the Lambda:
anywhere else and db.js would throw at runtime unless the packaging step changed too.
Values are DATA only - the tier ordering and the round-robin loop are still implemented
once per language (Python cannot execute JS), but both are driven entirely by what's here,
so tuning reasons/quota/prefixes needs no code change in either.
assignmentQuota was the one value that had already drifted: Python used 20 while the CRM
preview used 10, so the preview predicted assignments for half the real quota.
_reassignNote: Connected=No reassignment (scripts/assign_leads.py) and its 'Next to Assign' JS preview both read these four, so none of them can drift between the two the way assignmentQuota once did. reassignBacklogCutoff is a ONE-TIME migration boundary (a fixed date, not a rolling window) - a lead's own Calling Date must be on or after this for it to be eligible; chosen as 10 days before this feature shipped so the pre-existing backlog of already-Connected=No leads is left alone. reassignRetryCap is the total number of distinct agents ever allowed to try one lead (original assignment + reassignments) before it's left disposed for good. reassignMinHoldHours is a ROLLING window (unlike the cutoff above): a Connected=No lead is held with its current agent until this many hours have passed since it was actually assigned to them (lead_assignments.assigned_at, not Calling Date) - reassigning within minutes of the original assignment would strip a lead away before that agent had a fair shot at reaching the customer.
_reassignReserveNote: build_assignment_queue (scripts/lead_priority.py) and predictedAssignments (RtoCrmClient.js) both sort every fresh/never-touched lead ahead of every reassignment (excluded_by_row/excludedAgent), regardless of tier. With the RTO backlog routinely thousands of rows and quota only tens per run, the fresh pool never actually empties within one run, so without this reserve a reassignment eligible under reassignRetryCap/reassignMinHoldHours above never reaches the front of the cursor and sits attached to its Connected=No agent forever. reassignReservePerAgent holds back this many of each online agent's open quota slots for reassignment candidates BEFORE fresh claims them; taken only when a reassignment candidate actually exists that run (an empty reassignment pool leaves fresh with full capacity, unchanged from before this existed), and anything the reassignment pool doesn't use flows back to fresh in the same run rather than sitting idle. Fresh still outranks reassignment for the rest of each agent's capacity.
_highPriorityNote: Tier 1 - COD whose ORIGINAL system/courier RTO reason contains one of these (case-insensitive substring). The consignee has already refused or OTP-verified the cancellation, so the outcome is effectively known and worth acting on quickly. Prepaid is tier 0 and wins outright regardless of reason.
highPriorityCodRtoReasons: consignee opened the package and refused to accept
kyc|customer refused to share kyc/ ndc/ scd
_lowPriorityNote: Tier 3 - deliberately behind even 'every other COD order' (tier 2). These OTP outcomes are handled last in the assignment queue.
_awbPrefixNote: Delivery partner from an AWB code's prefix, first matching prefix wins. Business rule confirmed manually against known AWB ranges - nothing in the AWB format itself is self-describing.
